hints: You only need to change where each `next` points. Which node should each one point to?
Walk the list with two pointers: `prev` (already reversed) and `curr` (still to do).
Save curr.next first, then set curr.next = prev, then advance both pointers.

insight.oneLiner: Save next, flip curr.next to prev, advance - until curr is None; prev is the new head.

recall.q: What are prev and curr initialised to?

recall.a: prev - when curr becomes None, prev is the old tail, now the head.

signals: reverse a list or part of one
building block for reorder / k-group / palindrome-list problems
insight.why: Each node's pointer is flipped exactly once, in O(1) extra space. Saving next first keeps the unreversed part reachable.

oneLiner: Save next, flip curr.next to prev, advance - until curr is None; prev is the new head.

pitfalls.explain: Overwriting curr.next before saving it disconnects everything after curr. Save nxt = curr.next first.
pitfalls.title: Lost the rest of the list

pitfalls.explain: The old head must end up pointing to None; otherwise the first two nodes point at each other.
pitfalls.title: Left a cycle behind

footnotes.text: Recursion reverses the tail first; on the way back up, each node hooks itself behind its old successor. Uses O(n) stack space.

solutions.idea: Reverse the rest of the list recursively, then attach the current node at its end.
solutions.name: Recursion

footnotes.text: The order is the whole algorithm: save next, flip the pointer, advance. Flip before saving and the rest of the list is unreachable.

solutions.idea: Walk once, flipping each next pointer to the previous node.
solutions.name: Iterative pointer flipping
